## Review text

DOI: [10.7554/eLife.89962.3.sa2](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.89962.3.sa2)

In this work, Jarc et al. describe a method to decouple the mechanisms supporting progenitor self-renewal and expansion from feed-forward mechanisms promoting their differentiation.

The authors aimed at expanding pancreatic progenitor (PP) cells, strictly characterized as PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6.1+ cells, for several rounds. This required finding the best cell culture conditions that allow sustaining PP cell proliferation along cell passages while avoiding their further differentiation. They achieve this by comparing the transcriptome of PP cells that can be expanded for several passages against the transcriptome of unexpanded (just differentiated) PP cells.

The optimized culture conditions enabled the selection of PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6.1+ PP cells and their consistent, 2000-fold, expansion over ten passages and 40-45 days. Transcriptome analyses confirmed the stabilization of PP identity and the effective suppression of differentiation. These optimized culture conditions consisted in substituting the Vitamin A containing B27 supplement with a B27 formulation devoid of vitamin A (to avoid retinoic acid (RA) signaling from an autocrine feed-forward loop), substituting A38-01 with the ALK5 II inhibitor (ALK5i II) that targets primarily ALK5, supplementation of medium with FGF18 (in addition to FGF2) and the canonical Wnt inhibitor IWR-1, and cell culture on vitronectin-N (VTN-N) as a substrate instead of Matrigel.

The strength of this work relies on a clever approach to identify cell culture modifications that allow expansion of PP cells (once differentiated) while maintaining, if not reinforcing, PP cell identity. Along the work, it is emphasized that PP cell identity is associated to the co-expression of PDX1, SOX9 and NKX6.1. The optimized protocol is unique (among the other datasets used in the comparison shown here) at inducing a strong upregulation of GP2, a unique marker of human fetal pancreas progenitors. Importantly GP2+ enriched hPS cell-derived PP cells are more efficiently differentiating into pancreatic endocrine cells (Aghazadeh et al., 2022; Ameri et al., 2017).

The unlimited expansion of PP cells reported here would allow scaling-up the generation of beta cells, for the cell therapy of diabetes, by eliminating a source of variability derived from the number of differentiation procedures to be carried out when starting at the hPS cell stage each time. The approach presented here would allow selection of the most optimally differentiated PP cell population for subsequent expansion and storage. Among other conditions optimized, the authors report a role for Vitamin A in activating retinoic acid signaling in an autocrine feed-forward loop, and the supplementation with FGF18 to reinforce FGF2 signaling.

This is a relevant topic in the field of research, and some of the cell culture conditions reported here for PP expansion might have important implications in cell therapy approaches. Thus, the approach and results presented in this study could be of interest for researchers working in the field of in vitro pancreatic beta cell differentiation from hPSCs. results.result: The manuscript provides background on diabetes prevalence, etiology, and current treatment limitations, as well as developmental biology of pancreatic progenitors. These claims establish the clinical need and biological context for the study.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C23 are all supported by appropriate citations to prior literature or represent established medical/biological knowledge. These background claims provide necessary context but are not novel findings of this study.

results.result: Initial expansion conditions (CINI) using EGF, FGF2, and A83-01 resulted in inconsistent expansion of PP cells, with only occasional success (1 out of 5 attempts). When expansion occurred, PP marker expression was maintained and cells could differentiate into endocrine cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C29 are supported by experimental data including growth curves (Figure 1A), immunofluorescence, and qPCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). The low reproducibility (20% success rate) is clearly documented and motivates the subsequent optimization experiments.

results.result: RNA-Seq analysis comparing non-expanding and expanding PP cells under CINI conditions revealed that TGFβ signaling components were negatively correlated with expansion, while E2F targets and DNA replication were positively correlated. Specific ligands showed dramatic expression changes: TGFb1 and BMP2 were repressed ~4-fold, FGF18 was upregulated ~30-fold, and ALDH1A1 was downregulated ~25-fold.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C34 are supported by GSEA analysis (Figure 1D) and RNA-Seq data (Figures 1E-H, Supplementary file 1c). The transcriptomic approach to identify pathways associated with expansion is sound, though the sample size (n=3-4) is modest. The fold-change values are clearly documented.

results.result: Three modified conditions (C0, C1, C5) achieved reproducible PP cell expansion for at least 10-11 passages. C5 showed the fastest doubling time (2.3 days vs 3.6-3.9 days for C0/C1). All three conditions maintained expression of key PP markers PDX1, NKX6-1, and SOX9, while PTF1A expression was dramatically decreased. Flow cytometry confirmed ≥90% PDX1+/SOX9+ cells and ~40-50% PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6-1+ cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C40 are well-supported by growth curves with regression analysis (Figure 2A), qPCR data (Figures 2B-D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), immunofluorescence (Figures 2E-G), and flow cytometry (Figures 2H-K). Sample sizes are adequate (n=3-7) and statistical analyses are appropriate. The shift from multipotent to bipotent progenitor identity (C38) is a reasonable inference from PTF1A downregulation.

results.result: C5 expansion conditions promote PP cell proliferation more than survival. EdU incorporation was significantly higher in C5 (10.4±1.2%) compared to CINI (4.2±0.6%) cultures. Cell death appeared higher in CINI (22.1±5.0%) than C5 (17.2±4.7%) but did not reach statistical significance.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C43 are supported by EdU incorporation assays (n=4) and apoptosis assays (n=6) shown in Figure 3. The statistical analysis is appropriate, correctly noting that the difference in cell death did not reach significance. The conclusion that proliferation is the primary driver is reasonable given the significant difference in EdU incorporation.

results.result: Addition of canonical Wnt inhibitor IWR-1 to create condition C6 maintained similar growth kinetics (Td=2.5d) while significantly reducing liver marker expression and enriching PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6-1+ cells from 48±11% at p0 to 95±5% at p10. C6 cells could be cryopreserved with >85% survival, maintained chromosomal stability through 16 passages, and the procedure is GMP-compliant using VTN-N coating.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C49 and C69 are well-supported by growth curves (Figure 4A), qPCR (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), flow cytometry (Figures 4E-I), cryopreservation data (Figure 4J), and karyotyping (Figure 4—figure supplement 1M). Sample sizes are adequate (n=3-10). The GMP-compliance claim (C69) is a reasonable inference based on use of GMP-compatible reagents, though actual GMP production is not demonstrated.

results.result: RNA-Seq analysis of C6-expanded cells showed that PC1 explained 81% of variance and separated p0 from p5/p10 cells, with rapid transcriptome stabilization by p5. The expansion procedure resulted in strong upregulation of GP2 (50-fold higher than fibronectin-expanded cells), confirmed by immunofluorescence and flow cytometry (60±4.5% positive). PTF1A repression and suppression of endocrine differentiation programs were common features across all expansion methods.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C55 are supported by PCA analysis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), RNA-Seq data (Figures 5E-F, Supplementary file 1e), immunofluorescence, and flow cytometry. The comparative analysis with other published expansion methods strengthens the findings. GP2 upregulation is particularly notable as this marker is associated with enhanced endocrine differentiation potential.

results.result: C6 expansion conditions were successfully applied to H9 (female) and CRTD1 (male) hPS cell lines, achieving similar doubling times (2.2-2.3 days) and enrichment of PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6-1+ cells from 39-45% at p0 to 85-90% at p10.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C57 are supported by growth curve analysis (Figures 6A-B) and flow cytometry (Figures 6C-D). The demonstration of reproducibility across multiple cell lines of different sexes is important for generalizability. Sample sizes appear adequate though specific n values are not always clearly stated for all measurements.

results.result: Both directly differentiated (dPP) and expanded (ePP) cells from H1, H9, and CRTD1 lines differentiated into SC-islets with similar efficiency, containing 50-55% INS+ and GCG+ cells. Gene expression of endocrine markers and β-cell functionality assessed by GSIS were comparable between dPP- and ePP-derived SC-islets, with similar C-peptide secretion levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C63 are well-supported by immunofluorescence (Figures 7A-B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-B), flow cytometry (Figure 7C), qPCR (Figure 7D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1F), and GSIS assays (Figure 7E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1G). The demonstration that expanded cells retain differentiation potential and functionality is critical for the translational relevance of the expansion method.

results.result: The study demonstrates that combined stimulation of mitogenic pathways, suppression of retinoic acid signaling, and inhibition of selected TGFβ and Wnt signaling branches enables reproducible 2000-fold expansion of PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6-1+ PP cells over 10 passages (40-45 days) to ~90% homogeneity across multiple hPS cell lines. These expanded cells differentiate into functional SC-islets with efficiency comparable to non-expanded cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C68 are summary statements supported by the collective experimental data throughout the manuscript. The 2000-fold expansion calculation is consistent with the doubling time data and passage numbers. The claims accurately synthesize the major findings regarding expansion conditions, cell enrichment, and functional differentiation capacity.

results.result: Initial expansion attempts using CINI conditions (EGF, FGF2, and A83-01) resulted in growth arrest in most instances, with only occasional (1 out of 5) successful expansion maintaining PP identity and differentiation potential.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the initial CINI conditions as a starting point for optimization. The editor states the study describes 'a method to decouple the mechanisms supporting pancreatic progenitor self-renewal and expansion from feed-forward mechanisms promoting their differentiation,' implicitly accepting the baseline CINI data. No reviewer challenges these initial observations.

results.result: Transcriptomic comparison of expanding versus non-expanding PP cells revealed that TGFβ signaling components were negatively correlated with expansion, E2F targets and DNA replication were positively correlated, FGF18 was upregulated ~30-fold, and ALDH1A1 (RA-producing enzyme) was downregulated ~25-fold during successful expansion.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly recognize these transcriptomic findings as key mechanistic insights. One reviewer states the study 'unveiling crucial signaling pathways (eg TGF, Notch...) responsible for sustaining pancreas progenitors' and another notes 'a role for Vitamin A in activating retinoic acid signaling in an autocrine feed-forward loop, and the supplementation with FGF18.' The methodology is described as 'state-of-the-art' and 'robust.'

results.result: Optimized conditions C0, C1, and C5 enabled reproducible PP expansion for 10-11 passages with doubling times of 2.3-3.9 days, maintaining PDX1, NKX6-1, and SOX9 expression while dramatically decreasing PTF1A, suggesting a shift to bipotent endocrine/duct progenitor identity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings as demonstrating successful expansion with maintained PP identity. One reviewer notes 'the optimized culture conditions enabled the selection of PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6.1+ PP cells and their consistent, 2000-fold, expansion over ten passages.' The editor describes the evidence as 'convincing' with 'appropriate and validated methodology.'

results.result: C5 conditions promoted significantly more proliferation (10.4% EdU+ cells) compared to CINI (4.2% EdU+), with no statistically significant difference in apoptosis, indicating C5 primarily enhances proliferation rather than survival.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these mechanistic findings about proliferation versus survival. The methodology is described as 'state-of-the-art' and the dataset as 'robust,' implicitly accepting these proliferation and apoptosis measurements as valid evidence for the mechanism of action.

results.result: The optimized C6 condition (C5 plus IWR-1 Wnt inhibitor, using VTN-N substrate) maintained similar growth kinetics (Td=2.5d), significantly reduced liver marker expression, enriched PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6-1+ cells to 95% by p10, enabled cryopreservation with >85% survival, maintained chromosomal stability through 16 passages, and is GMP-compliant.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly recognize the GMP-compatibility as a major advance. One reviewer states the approach makes cells 'potentially suitable for GMP-compatible protocols' and represents 'a significant breakthrough for diabetes cell replacement therapies.' Another notes this addresses 'one of the current bottlenecks' in the field. The chromosomal stability and cryopreservation data are not challenged.

results.result: RNA-Seq analysis showed rapid transcriptome stabilization by passage 5, with all expansion procedures suppressing the endocrine differentiation program and PTF1A. The optimized method uniquely induced strong GP2 upregulation (~50-fold higher than other methods), with 60% of cells GP2+ by p10-12.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly highlight the GP2 upregulation as a key distinguishing feature. One reviewer states 'the optimized protocol is unique (among the other datasets used in the comparison shown here) at inducing a strong upregulation of GP2, a unique marker of human fetal pancreas progenitors' and notes 'GP2+ enriched hPS cell-derived PP cells are more efficiently differentiating into pancreatic endocrine cells.' The transcriptome analyses are described as confirming 'the stabilization of PP identity.'

results.result: The C6 expansion method was successfully applied to H9 and CRTD1 hPS cell lines, achieving similar doubling times (2.2-2.3 days) and enriching PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6-1+ cells from ~40-45% at p0 to 85-90% at p10.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the reproducibility across multiple cell lines as evidence of robustness. One reviewer notes the method works with 'PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6-1+ PP cells, derived from different, both XY and XX, hPS cell lines' and another states cells were 'derived from different hPS cell lines.' No concerns are raised about the cross-line applicability.

results.result: Both non-expanded (dPP) and expanded (ePP) cells from H1, H9, and CRTD1 lines differentiated into SC-islets with similar efficiency, containing 50-55% INS+/GCG+ endocrine cells with comparable marker expression and β-cell functionality as assessed by GSIS assays.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm that expanded cells retain differentiation potential. One reviewer notes the study provides 'clear explanations to the comments raised regarding quantifications, functionality of the cells' and another states 'expanded PP cells...were differentiated in microwells into homogeneous islet-like clusters (SC-islets) with very similar efficiency.' The functionality data is accepted without challenge.

results.result: The study demonstrates that combined stimulation of mitogenic pathways, suppression of RA signaling, and inhibition of TGFβ and Wnt pathways enables reproducible 2000-fold expansion of PDX1+/SOX9+/NKX6-1+ PP cells to ~90% homogeneity over 10 passages (40-45 days), which subsequently differentiate into functional β-cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers unanimously support this as the central finding. The editor calls it 'an important study' that 'describes a method to decouple the mechanisms supporting pancreatic progenitor self-renewal and expansion.' One reviewer states it 'represents a significant breakthrough for diabetes cell replacement therapies' addressing 'one of the current bottlenecks.' Another describes it as 'a clever approach' with 'strength' in identifying conditions that 'allow expansion of PP cells...while maintaining, if not reinforcing, PP cell identity.'

comparisons.comparison: Both evaluate claims C24-C29 regarding initial CINI conditions and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the experimental data (growth curves, immunofluorescence, qPCR) and documents the low reproducibility. Peer reviewers acknowledge these as valid baseline observations for subsequent optimization without challenging the findings.

Both evaluate claims C30-C34 regarding transcriptomic analysis and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the sound methodology with modest sample size (n=3-4). Peer reviewers explicitly recognize these as 'crucial signaling pathways' and describe the methodology as 'state-of-the-art' and 'robust,' providing stronger endorsement of the mechanistic insights.

Both evaluate claims C35-C40 regarding optimized expansion conditions and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval details the supporting data (growth curves, qPCR, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry) with adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'convincing' and accept the 2000-fold expansion and maintained PP identity as demonstrated.

Both evaluate claims C41-C43 regarding proliferation mechanisms and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval explicitly notes appropriate statistical analysis and the non-significant apoptosis difference. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings by describing the methodology as 'state-of-the-art' and dataset as 'robust' without raising challenges.

Both evaluate claims C44-C49, C69 regarding GMP-compatibility and stability and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the GMP claim is a reasonable inference based on reagent use rather than actual GMP production. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize GMP-compatibility as 'a significant breakthrough' and 'major advance,' providing stronger endorsement of translational potential.

Both evaluate claims C50-C55 regarding transcriptomic comparison and GP2 upregulation and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes GP2 upregulation as 'particularly notable' for endocrine differentiation potential. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight GP2 as 'a unique marker' and key distinguishing feature, emphasizing its importance for enhanced differentiation efficiency.

Both evaluate claims C56-C57 regarding reproducibility across cell lines and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the importance for generalizability but mentions sample sizes not always clearly stated. Peer reviewers accept cross-line applicability across both XY and XX lines without raising concerns about robustness.

Both evaluate claims C58-C63 regarding differentiation potential and functionality and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this demonstration as 'critical for translational relevance.' Peer reviewers explicitly affirm retained differentiation potential and accept functionality data, noting 'clear explanations' and 'very similar efficiency' in SC-islet formation.

Both evaluate claims C64-C68 regarding summary findings and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these accurately synthesize major findings with consistent expansion calculations. Peer reviewers provide unanimous strong support, calling it 'an important study,' 'significant breakthrough,' and 'clever approach' that addresses 'current bottlenecks' in the field.

OpenEval evaluates claims C1-C23 as background/context claims supported by prior literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than background claims.
